cards.speaker: Auditor Calla
cards.situation: Calla puts a slim ledger on your desk. Two ministries are off by nine million. Shall I write a name on the audit?

accept.outcome: Calla pencils a name in. The audit moves to the next desk by Tuesday.

decline.outcome: The ledger goes back into Calla's drawer. She updates the column in pencil and waits.

cards.speaker: Editor Halvik
cards.situation: News of the audit leaked overnight. Halvik holds the morning edition for a quote. Print a statement?

accept.outcome: Halvik prints six lines under your name. The bench reads the column at breakfast.

decline.outcome: Halvik prints the audit summary alone. The headline asks the question you didn't answer.

cards.speaker: Tax Commissioner Brask
cards.situation: Brask arrives with the revenue books. Nine million still missing while the headline asks who hid it. Reroute next quarter's spending?

accept.outcome: Brask redraws the lines. The road project pauses; the quartermaster will find out by Monday.

decline.outcome: Brask closes the book. The papers print the gap above the fold on Sunday.

cards.speaker: Treasurer Halen Vorr
cards.situation: With the audit shelved, the ledger still won't balance. Roll the nine million into next year's budget?

accept.outcome: Vorr writes the new line. The deficit is real but invisible. The papers will find it by Friday.

decline.outcome: Vorr reopens the file. The press desk hears about it within the hour.

cards.speaker: Magistrate Pell
cards.situation: After the press quote, a clerk arrives with a sealed envelope from the bench. The inquiry needs your signature. Open it?

accept.outcome: The inquiry opens. Halvik's desk lists the three witnesses by breakfast; the press has its case now.

decline.outcome: Pell files the envelope under the bench, marked for review next quarter.

cards.speaker: Selma
cards.situation: The hidden line has made the morning paper. Selma at the cafe wants to know if the nine million was hers. Answer her?

accept.outcome: You answer. Selma nods. The paper prints the answer the next day.

decline.outcome: Selma folds the paper. She walks the story to Halvik's desk before the cafe closes.

cards.speaker: Marshal Dren Volk
cards.situation: Kerovian scouts crossed at the river at dawn. The eastern barracks stand half-empty. Shall I call up the reserves?

accept.outcome: Whistles go up at every depot before nightfall. Twelve thousand boots board the train east.

decline.outcome: Volk salutes and goes to draft the public statement. The eastern bank stays quiet for now.

cards.speaker: General Marek
cards.situation: The reserves are at the depot, called up overnight. Six districts want their fathers home by Tuesday. Send them east?

accept.outcome: The trains roll east. The radio plays the anthem twice an hour.

decline.outcome: Marek discharges the reserves overnight. Six mayors call before breakfast asking for the papers in writing.

cards.speaker: Press Secretary Lindi
cards.situation: The six mayors want their fathers' discharge in writing. Lindi has a draft statement. Print hers under your name?

accept.outcome: Lindi's draft runs in the evening edition. The mayors now want the pension freeze lifted next.

decline.outcome: Lindi files the draft. The mayors hold a joint press call without you.

cards.speaker: Ambassador Hess
cards.situation: With the reserves stood down, Kerovia's ambassador wants a back-channel meeting tonight. Take the call?

accept.outcome: Hess takes the call. The river goes quiet by Thursday. Both flags fold up for the press.

decline.outcome: Hess hangs up without speaking. The columns drill again at dawn.

cards.speaker: Brigadier Ines
cards.situation: The eastern columns are deployed; three garrisons report no rifles. The quartermaster cites the missing audit. Buy from Vasalia?

accept.outcome: Vasalian crates dock at the southern harbour. Calla circles the entry in the ledger by lunchtime.

decline.outcome: Conscripts drill with broomsticks. The press finds the photograph by Wednesday.

cards.speaker: Aide-de-Camp Ren Halsey
cards.situation: After the back-channel, the Marshal's car is at the gate. The map room wants you in twenty minutes. Take the chair?

accept.outcome: You walk in. Volk gestures at the map. The decision is yours by midnight.

decline.outcome: You stay at the desk. Volk gives the morning interview alone; the editorials write themselves.

cards.speaker: Editor Halvik
cards.situation: Halvik holds the new press council bill. Every paper would licence through the ministry. Sign it?

accept.outcome: The bill goes through under your seal. Volk's adjutant phones at noon asking which papers his men can read on base.

decline.outcome: Halvik pulls the bill off the table. He prints a page-two editorial about it anyway.

cards.speaker: Press Secretary Lindi
cards.situation: With the bill signed, Lindi drafts the licensing forms. Three independent papers say they'll publish anyway. Approve the forms?

accept.outcome: The forms go out. By Monday the three papers have police at their doors.

decline.outcome: Lindi files the forms in her drawer. The three papers print twice on Saturday.

cards.speaker: Magistrate Pell
cards.situation: The bench will weigh the unsigned licensing forms next month. Pell asks if you'll brief her on the ministry's intent. Sit with her?

accept.outcome: You meet Pell. She files a narrow ruling that leaves the papers untouched.

decline.outcome: Pell rules without a briefing. The court asks Calla for the audit file before the next sitting.

cards.speaker: Counsel Aren
cards.situation: You blocked the licensing bill; the bench took up the press case Thursday. Aren wants a public defence in your name. Sign it?

accept.outcome: Aren delivers your defence to the bench. The case folds in nine minutes. The unions cheer outside.

decline.outcome: Aren shrugs and leaves. The bench reopens the licensing question.

cards.speaker: Editor Bjork
cards.situation: After the crackdown, Bjork prints the unredacted ministry memo on page one. The court wants the source list. Surrender it?

accept.outcome: Bjork hands over the list. Two desk editors are arrested before lunch.

decline.outcome: Bjork refuses. The interior pushes Defense to brief Volk on a public order option.

cards.speaker: Activist Niro
cards.situation: Your defence of the press emboldened the unions. Niro's thirty thousand have filled the square. Clear them by sundown?

accept.outcome: The cordon advances. The unions call a general strike for Monday; the pension desk braces.

decline.outcome: The cordon stands down. Niro thanks you on every public channel.

cards.speaker: Treasurer Halen Vorr
cards.situation: Vorr brings the pension bill. The line item costs more than the army's procurement. Freeze the index for one year?

accept.outcome: Vorr writes the freeze into the budget. Which cabinet voice reaches the desk first depends on the morning.

decline.outcome: Vorr stays in the chair until midnight reconciling lines. The freeze goes back in the drawer.

cards.speaker: Dr. Myra
cards.situation: With the freeze signed, three hospitals say their orderlies live on the pension. Waiting lists doubled last quarter. Subsidise the gap?

accept.outcome: Myra opens an emergency line. Calla wants the funding source on the audit page by Friday.

decline.outcome: Myra closes her folder. The hospitals run a skeleton shift through winter.

cards.speaker: Selma
cards.situation: With the freeze signed, Selma reads the notice at the cafe. Twelve pensioners gather behind her. Speak to them?

accept.outcome: You step outside. Selma counts the pensioners aloud, twelve becomes thirty by sundown.

decline.outcome: Selma reads the notice again, louder. The cafe owner brings the chair to the window.

cards.speaker: Tax Commissioner Brask
cards.situation: With the freeze signed, the revenue desk projects a four-percent bump in receipts. Brask wants to lock the gain into law. Approve?

accept.outcome: Brask drafts the lock-in. The treasury smiles for the first time this quarter.

decline.outcome: Brask folds the projection. The receipts climb regardless; the law stays open.

cards.speaker: Economist Ansa
cards.situation: Without the freeze, Ansa shows the deficit ladder hitting twelve million. The bonds desk is on the phone. Borrow it now?

accept.outcome: Ansa places the bond papers in front of you. Twelve million arrives by Tuesday.

decline.outcome: Ansa packs her files. The cabinet revisits the freeze next session.

cards.speaker: Selma
cards.situation: The freeze week ends. Selma unfolds a banner under your window; it reads NINE MILLION REMEMBERED. Speak to her?

accept.outcome: You step onto the balcony. Halvik's photographer prints the banner above the fold by morning.

decline.outcome: You stay inside. The banner stays up for two days. The paper prints the photo.

cards.speaker: Principal Vorn
cards.situation: With the loan in, Vorn says retired teachers are back at her school. Reading scores are climbing. Honour them publicly?

accept.outcome: You stand at the school gate at dismissal. By evening Calla wants the loan terms on the audit page.

decline.outcome: You stay at the desk. The reading scores climb without you in the photo.
